cards.name: SL Blue Ice (GoPro 3200k)
cards.summary: Icy cyan-blue grade: brighter mids with a blue-cyan cast, cool shadows and skies pushed to saturated cyan, while greens and reds keep their hue. This variant is for flat GoPro Protune footage shot under tungsten (3200K) light: its input LUT strongly cools the image first, so daylight or already-balanced footage turns heavily blue.
use_for: Stylised cold B-roll of winter, mountains or water
Futuristic tech mood shots in an AI explainer
Cold-palette montage in a reel or trailer
avoid: On daylight or already-balanced footage the 3200K input LUT adds a heavy blue cast (measured: neutral grey comes out strongly blue); use 'SL Blue Ice (Universal)' instead
Skin turns pale pink against cyan surroundings; avoid on interviews
Cyan skies look artificial in news footage
cards.equivalent: Lumetri Color with Input LUT 'GOPRO - 3200K - SL - PROFILE' + Look 'Blue Ice'
cards.scripting: Premiere's scripting API cannot apply .prfpset presets by name. The preset is one Lumetri Color (AE.ADBE Lumetri) with Basic Correction 'Input LUT' = SpeedLooks camera profile 'GOPRO - 3200K - SL - PROFILE' (Lumetri\LUTs\Legacy\GOPRO - 3200K - SL - PROFILE.itx) and Creative 'Look' = 'Blue Ice' (Lumetri\Looks\Legacy\Blue Ice.look, an identity Primary plus Lumetri\LUTs\Legacy\BLUE ICE - SL - 3527.itx; verified in the 2026 install), 'Intensity#2' 100, every other control at default. The file stores both as dropdown indices from an older list (Input LUT 23, outside the harvested 0-11 range; stored Look 6 from the old Legacy-looks list, which does not match the 2026 0-68 Look menu), and LUTAsset/LookAsset are strings a spec cannot set, so it cannot be rebuilt from pr_props. Unverified: the 2026 Input LUT list appears to come from Lumetri\LUTs\Technical (8 files) and does not include the camera profile, so when the preset is applied the camera stage may not load; check the Input LUT field after applying (the 2026 install still ships these exact files in Lumetri\LUTs\Legacy and Lumetri\Looks\Legacy, which suggests the old values are resolved). To get the exact grade: apply it by hand or copy attributes from a template clip, or bake it offline (convert the camera .itx and the look's .itx: ITX3, 40-byte header, 32^3 float32 RGB with red varying fastest, to .cube and chain two ffmpeg lut3d filters). For ordinary Rec.709 footage the Look dropdown also lists 'SL BLUE ICE' (Lumetri\LUTs\Creative\SL BLUE ICE.itx, apparently the version without the camera stage; pick it by name, the index is install-dependent). Approximation on Rec.709 footage: Lumetri Color {"Exposure": 0.5, "Temperature": -30, "Tint": -10, "Saturation": 110} (rough values from measuring the LUTs; verify by eye).

The preset is one Lumetri Color (AE.ADBE Lumetri) with Basic Correction 'Input LUT' = SpeedLooks camera profile 'GOPRO - 5800K - SL - PROFILE' (Lumetri\LUTs\Legacy\GOPRO - 5800K - SL - PROFILE.itx) and Creative 'Look' = 'Noir Nouvelle' (Lumetri\Looks\Legacy\Noir Nouvelle.look, an identity Primary plus Lumetri\LUTs\Legacy\NOIR NOUVELLE - SL - 3522.itx; verified in the 2026 install), 'Intensity#2' 100, every other control at default. The file stores both as dropdown indices from an older list (Input LUT 24, outside the harvested 0-11 range; stored Look 36 from the old Legacy-looks list, which does not match the 2026 0-68 Look menu), and LUTAsset/LookAsset are strings a spec cannot set, so it cannot be rebuilt from pr_props. Unverified: the 2026 Input LUT list appears to come from Lumetri\LUTs\Technical (8 files) and does not include the camera profile, so when the preset is applied the camera stage may not load; check the Input LUT field after applying (the 2026 install still ships these exact files in Lumetri\LUTs\Legacy and Lumetri\Looks\Legacy, which suggests the old values are resolved). To get the exact grade: apply it by hand or copy attributes from a template clip, or bake it offline (convert the camera .itx and the look's .itx: ITX3, 40-byte header, 32^3 float32 RGB with red varying fastest, to .cube and chain two ffmpeg lut3d filters). For ordinary Rec.709 footage the Look dropdown also lists 'SL NOIR NOUVELLE' (Lumetri\LUTs\Creative\SL NOIR NOUVELLE.itx, apparently the version without the camera stage; pick it by name, the index is install-dependent). Approximation on Rec.709 footage: Lumetri Color {"Saturation": 0, "Contrast": 10} (rough values from measuring the LUTs; verify by eye).

cards.name: SL Noir Nouvelle Red (GoPro 5800k)
cards.summary: Noir Nouvelle black and white with a mild red-filter channel mix: reds and skin render slightly lighter and blue skies slightly darker than in plain Noir Nouvelle (a subtle difference). This variant is for flat GoPro Protune daylight (5800K) footage: its input LUT roughly doubles saturation before the look, which in monochrome exaggerates the colour-filter separation (skin and reds versus skies and greens).
use_for: Monochrome portraits where skin should glow
Arty monochrome reel or trailer moments where faces should stay bright
avoid: On normal Rec.709 (non-Protune) footage the GoPro input LUT adds contrast (deeper blacks) and exaggerates the filter separation; use 'SL Noir Nouvelle Red (Universal)' instead
Red flags and banners render light grey and can merge with skin and sky tones
